0.0.n: A brief, friendly greeting here; it can also express thanks in other situations.

0.2.n: This is his family name, placed before his given name in Japanese.

0.3.n: 勇 is the first character of the given name 勇斗; read the two characters together as one name.

0.4.n: 斗 is the second character of the given name 勇斗, not a separate word here.

0.5.n: A polite ending used here to introduce himself by name.

1.0.n: A polite way to address the audience; さん adds respect.

1.1.n: The noun form of 気づく, with respectful お because he is referring to the audience noticing.

1.2.n: Links お気づき to 通り, forming the expression as you have noticed.

1.3.n: After a noun plus の, 通り indicates that something matches what was mentioned.

1.5.n: He introduces himself as the topic without adding the usual particle は.

1.7.n: Refers specifically to hair on the head; whose hair is understood from 私.

1.8.n: Marks 髪の毛 as what is being changed by the haircut.

1.9.n: Describes hair cut very short all over, not necessarily shaved completely bare.

1.10.n: Marks 丸刈り as the resulting state of his hair.

1.11.n: Polite past of させていただく, literally being allowed to do something; here it modestly announces his haircut.

2.0.n: Identifies the broadcast time of the television drama series.

2.1.n: Links 朝 to the following program description, identifying it as a morning series.

2.2.n: Part of 連続テレビ小説, describing a drama whose story continues across episodes.

2.3.n: Part of the program label 連続テレビ小説, rather than referring to a television set.

2.4.n: Usually means novel, but 連続テレビ小説 is a label for a serialized television drama.

2.6.n: This is the drama's title; the ordinary word おむすび means rice ball.

2.8.n: Marks the drama as the setting in which he plays the role.

2.9.n: Short for 高等学校; it modifies the following baseball description.

2.10.n: Combines with 高校 to specify the sport at high school level.

2.11.n: Commonly refers to school-age baseball players, especially those playing high school baseball.

2.12.n: Marks the baseball player as the role he portrays.

2.13.n: The plain nonpast form of 演じる refers here to an upcoming acting role.

2.14.n: Introduces the reason for the haircut explained in the next line.

3.0.n: Refers to his own head; Japanese leaves out my when ownership is clear.

3.1.n: Marks 頭 as the thing whose appearance he changed.

3.2.n: Names the short, all-over haircut that is the result of the action.

3.3.n: In the pattern を…にする, に marks the resulting state.

3.4.n: Polite past form of する; with 丸刈りに, it describes giving his head a buzz cut.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out I when introducing yourself with your name plus です.

1.lit: Everyone, as you have noticed, I humbly had my hair made into a buzz cut.
1.tip: させていただきました is a humble, polite way to announce what he did, not necessarily a claim of explicit permission.

2.lit: Because in the morning serialized television drama Omusubi, I will play a high school baseball player,
2.tip: ので gives a reason and connects this unfinished line to the haircut statement that follows.

3.lit: I made my head into a buzz cut.
3.tip: The pattern AをBにする means to change A into the state B.
